name: Dublin
operatingHours: Luas trams (Red and Green lines) run 5:30 AM–12:30 AM Mon–Fri, 6:30 AM–12:30 AM Sat and 7:00 AM–11:00 PM Sun and public holidays; no service on Christmas Day. Trams every 3–4 min at peak, 10–15 min off-peak. DART suburban trains run ~6:00 AM–~midnight.
fareInfo: With a TFI Leap Card the TFI 90 Minute Fare is €2 for unlimited Luas, Dublin Bus and most DART/commuter rail trips within 90 minutes (a cheaper short-hop fare applies for trips under ~3 km). Touch on before boarding and touch off on the Luas. Single paper tickets from Luas machines cost more. Leap Visitor Cards give unlimited travel for 1, 3 or 7 days, including Dublin Bus airport routes.

sights.name: Kilmainham Gaol
sights.note: The 1796 prison where leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising were held and executed, seen on a guided tour through its cells and the vaulted Victorian east wing.
sights.hours: ~9:30 AM–5:30 PM daily, guided tours only

sights.name: Guinness Storehouse
sights.note: A seven-floor visitor experience in a former fermentation building at St James's Gate brewery, ending with a pint in the rooftop Gravity Bar.
sights.hours: ~9:30 AM–7:00 PM daily, later in summer

sights.name: The Book of Kells Experience
sights.note: The 9th-century illuminated gospel book on display at Trinity College, with an exhibition on its making; the Long Room library is part-emptied during a multi-year conservation project.
sights.hours: ~8:30 AM–5:00 PM Mon–Sat, ~9:30 AM–5:00 PM Sun

sights.name: The Little Museum of Dublin
sights.note: A Georgian townhouse on St Stephen's Green filled with donated objects telling Dublin's 20th-century story, seen on lively guided tours.

sights.name: St Stephen's Green
sights.note: A Victorian park at the top of Grafton Street with a lake, bridges, flower beds and memorials, much loved for lunchtime breaks.

sights.name: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology
sights.note: Free museum on Kildare Street showing prehistoric Irish gold, the Ardagh Chalice and Tara Brooch, Viking finds and preserved bog bodies.

sights.name: The Irish Rock 'N' Roll Museum Experience
sights.note: A guided tour of working recording studios and memorabilia from Irish musicians such as U2, Thin Lizzy and Phil Lynott in Temple Bar.
sights.hours: ~10:30 AM–5:30 PM daily, tours on the hour

sights.name: Temple Bar
sights.note: The cobbled riverside quarter of pubs with live traditional music, small galleries and weekend food stalls; busy and pricey at night.

sights.name: Dublin Castle
sights.note: The former seat of British rule in Ireland, with lavish State Apartments, a medieval undercroft and the Chapel Royal; the gardens are free.

sights.name: Chester Beatty
sights.note: A free museum in the Dublin Castle grounds holding a collector's world-class hoard of manuscripts, Qur'ans, early Bibles and Asian prints.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–5:30 PM Mon–Sat (closed Mon Nov–Feb), from noon Sun

sights.name: Christ Church Cathedral
sights.note: Dublin's medieval cathedral, founded by the Vikings, with a huge 12th-century crypt; it connects by bridge to the Dublinia Viking museum.

sights.name: St Patrick's Cathedral
sights.note: Ireland's largest church, founded in 1191, where Jonathan Swift was dean; stained glass, monuments and a small park beside it.
sights.hours: ~9:30 AM–5:00 PM Mon–Sat, restricted hours Sun between services

sights.name: Jameson Distillery Bow St.
sights.note: The former Jameson distillery in Smithfield, now a guided tour and tasting on how Irish whiskey is made.

sights.name: 14 Henrietta Street
sights.note: A Georgian townhouse that became a crowded tenement, showing 300 years of Dublin home life on small-group tours.

sights.name: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum
sights.note: An interactive museum in the vaults of CHQ on the docks about the 10 million people who left Ireland and their influence worldwide.

sights.name: Glasnevin Cemetery
sights.note: Ireland's national cemetery, resting place of Daniel O'Connell and Michael Collins, with a museum and well-regarded guided tours.
sights.hours: Museum ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM daily; cemetery grounds longer

sights.name: Phoenix Park
sights.note: One of Europe's largest enclosed city parks, with roaming fallow deer, the Wellington Monument, Áras an Uachtaráin and Dublin Zoo.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; visitor centre ~9:30 AM–5:30 PM

railStations.name: Heuston Station
railStations.note: Terminus for Irish Rail intercity trains to Cork (~2.5 h), Galway, Limerick, Kilkenny and Waterford. Luas Red Line stop outside the entrance.
railStations.hours: Intercity trains ~6:00 AM–~9:30 PM by timetable; Luas 5:30 AM–12:30 AM weekdays.

railStations.name: Connolly Station
railStations.note: Dublin's busiest station: Enterprise trains to Belfast (~2 h 10 min), services to Sligo and Rosslare, plus DART and commuter trains. Luas Red Line stops at the station.
railStations.hours: Trains ~5:30 AM–~midnight by timetable; Luas 5:30 AM–12:30 AM weekdays.

airports.name: Dublin Airport
airports.transitNote: About 10 km north of the centre with no rail link, so nothing to the airport is on this map. Dublin Express and Aircoach coaches reach O'Connell Street in ~30–40 min; Dublin Bus routes 16 and 41 take the Leap fare but are slower. Taxis take ~25–40 min.
airports.hours: Coaches run ~24 hours (fewer overnight); Dublin Bus ~5:30 AM–~midnight.
